instrument_name: 2025 HB 1 'Build Up Mississippi Act' (signed version HB0001SG), amending Miss. Code 27-7-5
article_or_section: Section 1 (27-7-5(1)(b)(ii)); history: approved by Governor 2025-03-27 (billstatus HB0001.xml)
figure_or_rule_carried: Individual income tax: no tax on first 10,000 USD taxable income (since 2023); rate on taxable income above 10,000: 4.4% 2025, 4.0% 2026, 3.75% 2027, 3.5% 2028, 3.25% 2029, 3.0% 2030+; further cuts from 2031 conditional on Section 2 revenue triggers; tax stands repealed if rate reaches 0. Nonresidents taxed on MS-source net income (27-7-5(3)). Status: in force (enacted). Level: liability/assessment; withholding follows via DOR tables (2027 tables not yet published as of 2026-11-02).

instrument_name: MDOR Pub 89-700-25-1 (Rev. 07/25) Withholding Income Tax Tables and Employer Instructions, tables effective 2026-01-01 (file name revised1.13.2026)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exemptions: single 6,000; MFJ 12,000 (divisible in 500 multiples if both employed); head of family 9,500; dependent / age 65 / blind 1,500 each. Standard deduction: single 2,300; HoF 3,400; married 4,600 (both employed 2,300 each). Tax year 2026: 0% on first 10,000 taxable income, 4.0% above. Above-table wages: excess x 4% added to largest table figure; amount rounded to nearest whole dollar. No certificate -> zero exemption; federal W-4 not accepted (Form 89-350). Supplemental: aggregate (same time, or with current/last regular period, subtracting tax already withheld); if substantial over-withholding, may use highest bracket rate (4%). Wage-continuation sick pay = wages. Exempt from withholding: domestic service in private home, farm work, non-trade-or-business services, ministers. Resident working in another state: withhold MS unless other state requires withholding; nonresident: MS-service wages by earnings ratio; principal place MS -> total wages unless other state requires. Monthly/quarterly returns due 15th of following month (DOR sets frequency); TAP e-file mandatory at 10+ W-2s/1099s; W-2 EFW2 RS record due Jan 31; Form 89-140 with paper filers (<10); W-2 to terminated employee within 30 days; records 3 years; penalty 10%; interest per month on delinquent tax.

instrument_name: MDOR Computer Payroll Accounting - For Periods in 2026 (flowchart, Revised 8/13/25): official formula method / oracle
figure_or_rule_carried: Formula: AGP = period pay x periods (1/12/24/26/52/260 daily-misc); TI = AGP - (EX + STDED); STDED S 2,300, H 3,400, M 4,600, B (both employed) 2,300; TAX = 0 if TI <= 10,000 else (TI - 10,000) x 0.04; PWT = TAX / periods rounded to whole dollars; additional agreed amount added (whole dollars). G-DERIVE: Pub 89-700 Table A single weekly reproduced at the bracket upper bound (e.g. 450-460 at 0 exemption: (460 x 52 - 2,300 - 10,000) x 4% / 52 = 8.94 -> 9 = table; 8 test rows matched).

instrument_name: 35 Miss. Admin. Code Part III (Income and Franchise), Subpart 11 Withholding and Subpart 2 (gross income)
authority: Mississippi Department of Revenue (filed with Secretary of State)
article_or_section: 35.III.11 Ch.02 (101 supplemental), Ch.03 (exclusions: agricultural, domestic, ministers), Ch.07 (101-102 no-liability certificate), Ch.09 (resident/nonresident), Ch.11 (62-405 monthly if > 300/month; 62-400 quarterly), Ch.13 (corrections), Ch.15 (W-2 Jan 31 or 30 days after termination), Ch.16 (tables; computer formula); 35.III.2 (IRC 125/127/129; 27-7-16 deferrals)
figure_or_rule_carried: Supplemental paid separately: aggregate with current or last regular period; if tax withheld from regular wages, may withhold on supplemental as if no exemption claimed. Monthly return when withholding > 300/month, else quarterly with Commissioner approval; due 15th. No-liability exemption certificate (no liability prior and current year) effective through Apr 30 of next year. Resident: withhold on total wages except to extent withheld for another state; commuter to a no-income-tax state -> MS withholding on total. Nonresident: MS-service wages; base situs MS -> total. Employer may recover under-collection from later wages; over-collection repaid or remitted. IRC 125/127/129 benefits not subject to MS withholding; 27-7-16 tax-sheltered annuity / qualified retirement / deferred comp contributions excluded from gross income in year deferred; MS PERS contributions excluded.

instrument_name: MDOR Pub 89-145-25-1 (Rev 10/25) Procedures and Specifications for Filing Wage and Tax Information Electronically
article_or_section: Who must file; due dates; EFW2 RS record layout; state numeric code 28
figure_or_rule_carried: Electronic W-2 required if: federal e-file required, 10+ W-2s, 10+ 1099s, single payroll provider all year, or employee leasing company. W-2 e-file due Jan 31; 1099 due Feb 28. Format SSA EFW2 with RS record (state numeric code 28); EFW2C corrections; 1099/W-2G per IRS Pub 1220. Non-compliance minimum penalty 250 USD. Edition: 2025 filing season (Rev 10/25), used for W-2s filed early 2026; TY2026 edition not yet seen.

instrument_name: Mississippi State Directory of New Hires - New Hire Reporting Law page (operated for MDHS Division of Child Support Enforcement)
authority: Mississippi Department of Human Services (State Directory of New Hires)
article_or_section: Law page; cites Miss. Code 43-19-46 and 93-11-101 and 42 U.S.C. 653a
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers report newly hired and re-hired employees to the State Directory within 15 days of hire date (Miss. Code 43-19-46; 93-11-101; PRWORA). Penalty up to 25 USD per unreported new hire; up to 500 USD where employer-employee conspiracy. Use the same FEIN as on the quarterly wage report. Statute text itself not read (Miss. Code on Lexis public access, not fetched).

instrument_name: Mississippi State Directory of New Hires - Reporting Fundamentals (who, what, when, how)
authority: Mississippi Department of Human Services (State Directory of New Hires)
article_or_section: Who is required to report; What do I have to report
figure_or_rule_carried: Report employees who reside or work in MS (even one day); re-hires after a break of at least 60 consecutive days; temp agencies report once. Required employee fields: name, mailing address, SSN, date of hire, date of birth, gender, salary, payment frequency, medical insurance eligibility. Required employer fields: FEIN (same as on UI wage report), name, address, state EIN. Optional: middle initial, phone, contact, email, payroll country code. Channels: online (ms-newhire.com), electronic file, paper form or W-4; multistate employers may designate one state.

instrument_name: MDHS Division of Child Support Enforcement - Reference Guide for Employers and Income Withholders
authority: Mississippi Department of Human Services, Division of Child Support Enforcement
article_or_section: pp.5-7: income withholding, fees, CCPA limits, priority, lump sums
figure_or_rule_carried: IWO: begin no later than first pay period after 14 days from receipt; remit to SDU within 7 working days of withholding; notify on termination. Fees: employer may withhold 2.00 USD per month processing fee from employee (interstate: work-state law governs fee); also withhold and send a 5.00 USD administrative fee to the SDU. Limits = CCPA 50/60%, +5% (55/65%) if arrears > 12 weeks. Arrears at least 20% of current support unless ordered otherwise. Priority: child support above all garnishments/attachments/assignments; only federal tax liens entered before the order rank ahead; multiple orders pro rata. Lump sums > 500 USD (bonus, commission, severance, vacation payout): notify MDHS 45 days before payment when the order includes arrears; hold until 30 days after intended date or MDHS authorization. Guide dated 2020 (upload path); current edition not confirmed.

instrument_name: 2013 HB 141 (as sent to Governor), codified Miss. Code 17-1-51: local minimum/living wage and vacation/sick-day mandates prohibited
figure_or_rule_carried: No county or municipality may establish a mandatory minimum/living wage rate or a minimum number of vacation or sick days, paid or unpaid, that regulates how a private employer pays its employees; the matter is reserved to the Legislature (25-3-40). Consequence: no local minimum wage and no local paid-sick-leave ordinance can apply to private employers in MS. Approval date 2013-03-25 per tier-B lead (LegiScan); effective date read in Section 4 of the act.

instrument_name: US DOL Wage and Hour Division - State Minimum Wage Laws (Mississippi entry)
authority: U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division
article_or_section: Mississippi entry (page updated 2026-07-01; same file as US-TNS5-011)
figure_or_rule_carried: Mississippi: no state minimum wage law. Employers subject to the FLSA must pay the federal minimum wage of 7.25 USD/hour. No 2027 state rate (no state law).

instrument_name: Mississippi Employment Security Law (MDES compilation of Miss. Code Title 71 ch.5, web edition 2024-02-15): coverage 71-5-11, contributions 71-5-351, taxable wages 71-5-353(4)
authority: Mississippi Department of Employment Security (compilation of statute)
figure_or_rule_carried: Contributions due quarterly by the last day of the month after the quarter; never deductible from wages (71-5-351(1)); optional Mississippi Level Payment Plan (bank draft schedule May 15 / Aug 15 / Nov 15 / Jan 31). Fractions of a cent: < 0.5 cent dropped, >= 0.5 rounded up. Taxable wage base 14,000 USD per employee per calendar year since 2011 (7,000 through 2010-12-31), counting wages paid by employer or predecessor; 'employment' includes service under another state's UC law -> wages reported to another state count toward the MS base. Localization test (base of operations / direction / residence) in 71-5-11 I(8)-(10). Coverage: agricultural labor only if cash wages >= 20,000 in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks; domestic service if >= 1,000 cash in a quarter; excluded: casual labor, child under 21 employed by parent, parent/spouse employment, federal employment, railroad, 501(a) org if < 50/quarter, students employed by their school, ministers (71-5-11 J). Edition 2024-02-15: 2025/2026 amendments not checked.

instrument_name: MDES Quarterly Report and Tax Due Dates page
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly wage reports (UI-3) and tax (UI-2) due by last day of month after quarter: Q1 Apr 30, Q2 Jul 31, Q3 Oct 31, Q4 Jan 31; weekend -> next business day. File and pay online after registration (MDES online system), or mail to PO Box 22781 Jackson MS 39225-2781. Refunds in writing.

instrument_name: MDES Wage Reporting Requirements on Magnetic Media (ICESA Format - Year 2012 compliant, Revised 02/2012) and Magnetic Media Specifications page
article_or_section: Section I (required fields), Section II (file), Appendix A (ICESA layout)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI-3 wage report file: ICESA code 'S' employee record, 275-character records, CR/LF delimiters, file name UIWAGE.TXT; MDES also accepts the EFW2 (MMREF-1) RS record with required positions 1-2 'RS', 3-4 FIPS numeric code, 10-18 SSN, 19-33 first name, 34-48 middle name, 49-68 last name, 197-202 reporting period, 203-213 state quarterly UI total wages, 248-267 state employer account number. Money fields numeric, implied decimal, no negatives. Physical media (diskette/CD) wording is dated (2012); online filing on the MDES system is the current channel. Bulk UI-2 (tax report) filing: CD upload for preparers with 25+ clients (separate page).

instrument_name: MDES Bulk Filing (Form UI-2 Tax Report only) page
figure_or_rule_carried: Bulk filing of UI-2 tax reports for preparers with 25+ clients: CD upload, file name UI2_PAYROLLCompanyName_yyyyMMdd.txt, test CD 14 days prior, one super-check, current quarter only, clients must hold MDES EAN; UI-3 wage detail filed separately by the prescribed electronic method.

instrument_name: US DOL WHD - State Payday Requirements (Mississippi row and footnote 12; page revised 2023-01-01)
authority: U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division
article_or_section: Mississippi row (bi-weekly / semi-monthly) and footnote 12 (same file as US-UTS5-009)
figure_or_rule_carried: Mississippi payday rule (Miss. Code 71-1-35, per DOL summary): applies only to entities engaged in manufacturing employing 50 or more employees and employing public labor, and to public service corporations; pay once every two weeks or twice each calendar month (public service corporations: semimonthly, wages earned within 15 days of payment). No general pay-frequency rule for other private employers. Statute text not read (Miss. Code on Lexis public access); DOL page revised 2023-01-01.

instrument_name: Mississippi Legislature - 2026 Regular Session Report of All Measures (last change 2026-06-22) - bulletin sweep
article_or_section: All measures with last action 'Approved by Governor', filtered on income tax / wage / employment / unemployment / garnishment / leave / child support / retirement keywords
figure_or_rule_carried: Sweep 2026-01-01..2026-11-02: no 2026 act changes the PIT rate, withholding, minimum wage, UI wage base, paid leave or pay-statement rules. Died in committee: HB 204 (exclude overtime pay from income), HB 543 and HB 741 (state minimum wage 10.00). Enacted payroll-adjacent: HB 4073 Mississippi Work and Save Program (voluntary state Roth payroll-deduction IRA; see US-MSS5-017); SB 2369 (child support: withhold gaming winnings, not wages); HB 343, SB 2867, SB 3228 (employer income tax credits: ICHRA, child care, skills training - not payroll withholding). Status of each from the measure list's last action.

instrument_name: 2026 HB 4073 (as sent to Governor; approved 2026-04-08): Mississippi Work and Save Program (state-sponsored payroll-deduction Roth IRA); revises certain PERS provisions
figure_or_rule_carried: Status: enacted (approved by Governor 2026-04-08 per measure list); Sections 17-18 in force 2026-03-01, rest 2026-07-01. Employer participation is VOLUNTARY: 'covered employer' = private employer without a tax-favored retirement plan in current or 2 prior years that voluntarily participates; employees 18+ with MS-allocable wages. Payroll-deduction Roth IRA, automatic enrollment with opt-out permitted; Treasurer may set auto-escalation up to +1%/year to max 8%. Participating employers withhold and remit employee contributions. Contributions to begin no later than 2028-08-01 (phase-in completed by 2028-07-01). Level: employer payroll deduction (post-tax Roth), only if the employer opts in. Default contribution rate not fixed in the statute text read.

instrument_name: 2010 HB 583 (as sent to Governor; approved): breach of security notice (codified Miss. Code 75-24-29)
figure_or_rule_carried: Any person doing business in MS that owns, licenses or maintains personal information (name + SSN, driver licence/state ID number, or financial account/card number with access code) of MS residents must notify affected individuals of a breach of unencrypted data without unreasonable delay (unless no likely harm after investigation); data maintainers notify the owner; law-enforcement delay allowed; written, telephone or electronic notice. Payroll records (SSN, bank account) fall in scope. Effective date 2011-07-01 read in the act's effective-date section; codification as Miss. Code 75-24-29 is a tier-B lead. No MS rule on SSN truncation on pay statements found.

instrument_name: MDOR Business Tax Frequently Asked Questions - Withholding Tax section
article_or_section: Withholding Tax; Filing Withholding Returns; Registration and Updating Account Information
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee refusing Form 89-350: withhold as single, no exemptions. Employer must send DOR a copy of any certificate claiming more than 10 allowances or 'exempt' where wages normally exceed 200 USD/week. MS resident working in another state with an income tax: employer withholds for the other state, not MS (credit at assessment). Nonresident working in MS: withhold on MS-service wages unless MS earnings for the year will be less than the standard deduction for the filing status. Withheld in wrong state: reimburse employee and amend. Reservation Indian living and working on reservation exempt with Form 80-340. Pensions/annuities not subject to MS withholding. Domestic help in the home exempt. Section 125 pre-tax. Corporate officers = employees. Severance taxable. Bonus with regular wages: aggregate. Tips paid directly by customers not subject to withholding (still taxable); tips paid through employer subject. Family members including children under 18 subject. Returns due 15th; monthly if average liability >= 300 USD/month, else quarterly; no depository system (pay with return); e-file and e-pay mandatory if liability >= 20,000 USD in any period; late payment penalty 10% + interest 1/2% per month; W-2C copy to DOR if MS wages/withholding change; no W-2 filing extensions; records 3 years (payroll, employee list, salaries, SSNs, addresses). Registration via TAP: required for employers doing business in MS, paying MS residents anywhere, or paying nonresidents for MS services; 8-digit MS account number (not FEIN); new account if FEIN changes or business purchased. 1099/info returns: report personal-service income over 3,000 USD.
